summary: WI-763 direction and boundary are coherent (PR-local approval is bound to authored `work_item.review_entry`, raw/shadow/runtime evidence cannot satisfy approval, and `controlled-merge` consumes required-check readback before delegating). However, the current worktree cannot be treated as formally approved for merge gating because the authored implementation review record `.loom/reviews/WI-763.json` is stale relative to the current HEAD `ba5dc4bacaf9`, causing `checkpoint merge` to fail closed and preventing `pr-gate` from proving fresh approval for the current head.

findings.summary: `checkpoint merge` fails closed because the authored implementation review record `.loom/reviews/WI-763.json` is stale for the current HEAD (`reviewed_head` is pinned to `a547ff0d...` while non-carrier implementation changes exist after that head). Until a fresh authored review is recorded for the current HEAD (or the head-binding contract is updated to cover the actual post-review changes), `pr-gate` cannot provide PR-head approval truth for host enforcement.

disposition.summary: Re-author `.loom/reviews/WI-763.json` against current HEAD `ba5dc4bacaf9` (and re-run the local validation summarized in the record), then confirm `python3 tools/loom_flow.py checkpoint merge --target . --item WI-763` returns `pass` before treating PR gating as satisfied.

findings.details: category: new; evidence: `checkpoint merge` reports `review artifact is stale for the current HEAD`, so the approval truth is not fresh for the current implementation head.

findings.summary: `.loom/progress/WI-763.md` claims only carrier-only drift exists after the reviewed head, but `checkpoint merge` currently blocks on stale review artifact, indicating post-review changes exceed the allowed carrier set for head-binding freshness. This mismatch risks operators believing PR gating is ready when it is not.

disposition.summary: Update `.loom/progress/WI-763.md` to reflect the current merge-checkpoint truth (stale review artifact) until a new authored review record is bound to the current HEAD and `checkpoint merge` passes.

findings.details: category: new; boundary: recovery surface should not contradict gate-chain freshness checks.

findings.summary: Host enforcement for `loom-pr-merge-gate` is not yet proven by live GitHub readback (required check via branch protection or active ruleset, plus a real PR-head run); repo-local workflow presence and local validation are not sufficient to claim “host-enforced” closure for the PR #762 regression class.

disposition.summary: Collect and record fresh host readback evidence that `loom-pr-merge-gate` is required on `main` (branch protection and/or ruleset) and that the check ran for the target PR head SHA.

findings.details: category: unresolved; boundary: requires host state readback outside the repo tree.

findings.summary: The required check workflow checks out and executes repository code from the PR head (`python3 tools/loom_flow.py ...`). This is acceptable for trusted contributor sets, but it is a security/trust boundary decision if untrusted external PRs can trigger the required check.

disposition.summary: Document and enforce contributor trust assumptions before making `loom-pr-merge-gate` required (or redesign the workflow to avoid executing arbitrary PR-head code via pinned tooling / API-fetched artifacts).

findings.details: category: new; boundary: host-required check executes PR-supplied code with a read-scoped token.

findings.summary: The host workflow is triggered only on `pull_request`. If the repository uses GitHub merge queue, required checks must also trigger on `merge_group` or the host-enforced gate can be skipped/never reported for merge-queue merge groups.

disposition.summary: Decide whether Loom self-governance supports merge queue; if yes, add `merge_group` trigger (and validate required-check naming/readback under merge queue) before treating host enforcement as complete.

findings.details: category: new; boundary: host enforcement behavior differs between direct PR merge and merge queue unless `merge_group` is supported.
